messages:
maria-support: FYI a customer reported a streaming response that ends abruptly — client sees an incomplete JSON object and no finish_reason. Happened during an API key rotate on their side. request_id: r-0a1b2c3d model: redwood-large region: us-west-2

josh-eng: Can you paste the raw SSE output the client got? Also early/late timestamps for the auth swap?

maria-support: Repro steps I used:
1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <temp-token>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"long text"}'
2) while streaming, rotate token (simulate client refresh)

Raw SSE fragment we observed (truncated):
-----BEGIN-SSE-----
data: {"id":"r-0a1b2c3d","object":"text_stream","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...lots of text..."}}, {"delta":{"content":"more text"}} , {"delta":{"content":"final chunk\n"}},
data: {"choices":[{"finish_reason":
-----END-SSE-----

Note the stream closes right after "finish_reason" key starts — the trailing value and closing braces are missing.

olivia-runtime: That looks like a truncated TCP/connection close at the same time we were doing auth handoff. Any proxy/nginx logs from the customer's side or our edge?

maria-support: We grabbed the customer's edge logs; snippet from their load balancer around the same time:

[2026-03-15T17:22:34.123Z] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
[2026-03-15T17:22:34.124Z] client: 10.24.5.6, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.1.2.3:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"

They say their token rotate occurs ~17:22:34.

josh-eng: Two hypotheses: 1) upstream (our runtime) closed the socket mid-emit due to worker restart or OOM; 2) their proxy closed the connection on seeing auth refresh/401 and didn't allow the final event through. Do we have worker logs around r-0a1b2c3d?

olivia-runtime: Pulling runtime logs now. Found these on the host serving that request:
[INFO] emit final event for r-0a1b2c3d size=812 bytes
[WARN] client closed connection while writing chunk after 120ms

That suggests the server attempted to send the final event but the socket write returned EPIPE. Need kernel socket trace to confirm.

maria-support: Customer also says they never saw a 4xx from the server — their client just drops to closed stream. They implied their SDK auto-swapped auth header at exactly the same moment.

eng-oncall: Two practical asks: 1) can we reproduce internally by forcing token rotate mid-stream (we should), 2) can we build a short wrapper test that does a graceful resume via the resume header to see if the final chunk is recoverable? If not, escalate.

josh-eng: Quick workaround for customers: retry on abrupt connection close and request a resume using the resume header (if present). But important: if the final object is truncated and not present in the resume, we need runtime-level fix to ensure we flush the terminal object before shutting down workers during auth/rotate events.

maria-support: Created ticket INC-2026-789 and linked customer logs and the curl repro. support-bot: :ticket: INC-2026-789 created and assigned to eng-runtime.

eng-oncall: Assigning to olivia-runtime. Olivia, can you instrument a short test that simulates a midstream auth header swap and captures kernel-level EPIPE vs upstream close? Also check if keepalive/idle timeout on our ELB can cause similar mid-chunk closures.

olivia-runtime: Will do. I’ll set up a reproducible harness and post results here. If I can reproduce I'll add a small guard to delay worker shutdown until final chunk acknowledged or add an explicit final-flush on write errors.

josh-eng: Thanks — if you find a specific edge (proxy sees 401 and closes), add guidance to support playbook: detect token rotate windows and prefer resume+retry semantics.

maria-support: Customer updated they can tolerate retry for now but want a long-term fix. I scheduled a live debug session tomorrow 10:00 PST.

eng-oncall: Marking thread as escalated. Please paste test results here when you have them. :mag_right:
